title: The dev servers the projects on this machine describe
description: GET /v1/devstacks: the input bar's server list (⌘S), which the Swift app draws natively from `DevStack.swift` and `Controller.refreshStacks`. A project describes its stack in a `.devstack.json` at its root (docs/devstack.md in the Swift app's repository). The projects looked at are the ones the Swift app looks at: every directory `~/.claude/project-icons.json` names, and every live session's working directory, each walked up to the home directory for the file. **This daemon never runs a command that file names** — not `status`, and not `up`, `down`, `restart` or `logs`. The Swift app ran them only from its own native window, after a person had trusted the file's exact bytes; here every route is reachable by every paired device, and a route that runs a repository's commands would be code execution for all of them. So state is only what can be learned without running anything: whether something is listening on each port the file declares.

DevStackState.description: `running`: every declared process answered. `partial`: some did. `stopped`: none did. `unknown`: nothing could be asked without running one of the project's commands, and `unknown` is never reported as `stopped` — a live site under a mark that says it is down is worse than no mark.

DevStackUnknown.description: Why a stack's state is `unknown`. `status_not_run`: the file names a `status` command and declares no ports, so only running that command could tell, and this daemon does not run it. `nothing_declared`: the file names neither.

DevStackCommand.description: A command a `.devstack.json` names. Listed so a reader can say which ones exist; none of them is run here.

DevProcessState.description: The Swift app's six words for one process. A port probe can only say `running` (something accepted a connection on 127.0.0.1) or `stopped` (nothing did, or the process declares no port to ask); the other four come from a `status` command, which is not run here.

DevProcess.description: One process the file declares under `processes`.

port.description: The port it listens on, as declared. Absent when the file gives none.

url.description: The address the file gives for it, when it gives one — often a tunnel or a local hostname rather than the port.

name.description: The file's `name`, else the name of the directory it is in.

root.description: The directory the file was found in.

commands.description: The commands the file names, in this order: status, up, down, restart, logs, attach. None of them is run.

DevStacksReply.description: Every stack found, sorted by name and then by directory. A linked Git worktree found only through the icon registry is left out: it is a copy of a project already on the list, and the Swift app drew one indistinguishable row for each.

observedAt.description: When the ports were asked, in seconds since 1970.

truncated.description: The search stopped before every known directory was looked at, or more stacks were found than one answer carries. Absent when nothing was left out.
